evidence: src/infrastructure/UserController.ts setupRoutes(): Router().post/get with req/res handling is HTTP transport, which fits infrastructure
POST /users hands creation to this.createUserUseCase.execute(name), so the creation logic stays in the application layer
`if (!name) res.status(400)` is request-shape validation at the transport boundary, not a business rule
GET /users calls this.userRepository.findAll() and maps getId()/getName() into a response object. This is a presentation mapping with no business rule, though it skips a use case (borderline)
parsedVerdict.reasoning: UserController is an Express transport adapter in the infrastructure layer. Its responsibilities are route registration, request parsing, HTTP status and JSON response handling, and translating errors into HTTP responses. All of these are infrastructure (transport) concerns. Creating a user is handed to CreateUserUseCase, so the creation logic stays in the application layer. The `if (!name)` check is request-shape validation that returns a 400, which is normal for a controller and not a business rule. The GET /users handler queries the repository directly and maps entities to a plain response object. The mapping is presentation work and the query has no business rule, but orchestrating a query without going through a use case is borderline. Whether a controller may call the repository directly is a layer-dependency question and out of scope. No domain logic, persistence implementation or business rule is misplaced in this file.
